title: case-021 · History notebook · A food counter on the street
blocks: A food counter on the street
The game represents a counter and inset jar forms. This is a schematic model of the food-counter setting.
The in-game counter is an original schematic reconstruction, not an archaeological photograph.
The thermopolium, or food-and-drink counter, of Vetutius Placidus had large storage jars built into its serving counter.
The Park describes the surviving counter and its embedded vessels.
A counter does not establish its exact daily menu or the identity of everyone who worked there.
Sabina, her stock, prices and the flour dispute are fictional. The model is not a surveyed reconstruction.
Which visible feature suggests that customers were served here?
Original prose and schematic game geometry. No external image reproduced.
Archaeological Park of Pompeii: Along the streets of Pompeii · https://pompeiisites.org/en/pompeii-map/analysis/along-the-streets-of-pompeii/

title: case-022 · History notebook · A home turned into a workplace
blocks: A home turned into a workplace
The game represents washing basins inside a simplified workshop.
The game basins are schematic geometry, not a measured plan.
The Fullonica of Stephanus was a cloth-cleaning workshop adapted from a house. Fullonica means a fullery, where cloth was processed.
Washing facilities and changes to the domestic building support its workshop interpretation.
The conventional building name does not establish every occupant or worker. Precise ownership can be an interpretation.
Chreste, her schedule and the paid shifts offered to Aelia are invented. Chreste is enslaved; Aelia taking a paid shift is a different situation.
What would distinguish a workshop from a room used only for domestic life?

title: case-023 · History notebook · A person who had been freed
blocks: A person who had been freed
Aelia is a fictional freedwoman: she was enslaved and was later freed.
Naevoleia Tyche’s commemorative monument and inscription identify her as a freedwoman.
The Park discusses the inscription on the monument near the Herculaneum Gate. That monument is outside this game district.
One prominent monument cannot show how every freedwoman lived. Women had varied social statuses and opportunities. The Park’s imagined first-person narration is modern interpretation.
Aelia is not Naevoleia Tyche. Her money, work, access and choices are fictional simplifications, not general Roman legal rights.
Can one prosperous individual stand for everyone who had been freed?
Original prose and schematic game geometry. No external image reproduced.
